issue: लज्जा मेरी हाथ तिहारे । पड़ा हूँ चरण सहारे: the second half is about four mātrās short of a chaupāī half (16); a word may be lost. The book and Drik Panchang print it alike, and a web search found no other copy.
देखत सुन नर मुनि मन मोहे: सुन (hearing) sits oddly in the stock phrase; सुर नर मुनि (gods, men and sages) may be meant. Both witnesses print सुन.
our reading: देखत सुन: on seeing it and hearing of it, men and sages are enchanted.
alternatives: सुर नर मुनि: the minds of gods, men and sages are enchanted on seeing it.

issue: लाल देह सिन्दूर बदन में: whose body is red is not named; it follows the burly messengers of chaupāī 29.
our reading: The messengers: their bodies are red, with vermilion on them.
alternatives: Pretarāja himself (or Hanumān, Bālājī) red with vermilion.

issue: विमल वेश अंजिन सुवन प्रेतराज बल धाम: one person or two? The Mehandipur shrine has both Hanumān (Bālājī) and Pretarāja.
our reading: Two addressed together: the son of Añjanī (Hanumān), of pure attire, and Pretarāja, abode of strength.
alternatives: Pretarāja alone, called by Hanumān's epithet: Pretarāja, son of Añjanī, of pure attire, abode of strength.
